translations.answer: No. The author still believes the 'period' parameter is incorrect after excluding I2C jitter; maintainers cannot reproduce it on a regular PC and require printing 'current_time', 'previous_time', and 'measured_period' within the 'ros2_control' node. The thread ends here, so only diagnostic steps are retained, and no root cause or fix for the period calculation error is provided.
translations.applicability: Recorded on Raspberry Pi 5; missing precise ros2_control version and maintainers have not reproduced it.
translations.credibility.rationale: The answer has not been closed or there is a conflict; only problem clues are formed; no reproducible reproduction record is formed.
translations.details.attempts.0: Configure realtime group limits; use chrt to adjust process and child process priority; disable I2C IMU read; maintainers suggest printing time variables at the same location.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First, remove or isolate I2C IMU read to observe if control cycle jitter disappears.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Do not use the same phenomenon to qualitatively define 'period' parameter; print 'current_time', 'previous_time', and 'measured_period' in the same location within the 'ros2_control' node.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: For cyclic jitter, remove or isolate the I2C IMU read after which the author observed cyclic stability.
translations.details.environments.0: Raspberry Pi 5; controller_manager at 250 Hz; low-latency kernel; realtime group limits configured afterward; no precise ROS 2/ros2_control version provided.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread does not explain using asynchronous I/O, independent thread, or specific driver fix; only confirms stability after stopping.
translations.details.limits.1: Cannot directly extrapolate low-latency kernel results to all hardware and RT kernels.
translations.details.outcomes.0: I2C-induced jitter has been confirmed by author A/B; the 'period' parameter issue has not closed.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How should I2C read and 'update(period)' parameter be diagnosed when ros2_control 250 Hz cycle has large jitter?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not let sensor read cause unbounded blocking of real-time control thread; monitor worst-case execution time and deadline miss.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Author confirms large jitter comes from I2C IMU read; 'period' parameter issue remains undiagnosed.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Actual time difference fluctuates between ~1.1-6.9 ms; 'update()' period parameter does not match the author's offline time difference.
translations.source.title: ros2_control control cycle high jitter and 'update(period)' period anomaly must be separated for diagnosis
